PRADESH)
 
 (STATE BY SHRI PRADEEP GUPTA - GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE )
 (OBJECTOR BY SHRI BRIJESH MISHRA - ADVOCATE WITH SHRI SUBHAM  MISHRA - ADVOCATE)

This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant for grant of regular bail relating to F I R No.353/2023 dated 02.08.2023, registered at P.S.- Suhagpur, District Shahdol (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420/34 of IPC.

Applicant is in detention since 13.08.2023.
2.

As per the prosecution story, on 02.08.2023, Mohit Gupta submitted an application in writing alleging that he had some conversation with Ashish Rajak, who informed that 10 Billion Company makes the amount double in 200 days.

He spread this information among his friends Prakash,
Rajan, Sunil, Manoj and Brajendra Dwivedi.
They all met with Ashish Rajak and thereafter on the basis of account number given by Ashish Rajak, they invested amount through RTGS and cash.

sentences.text: After completion of the period of 200 days, Ashish refused to return/refund the money.
After investigation, charge-sheet was filed.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that applicant has already deposited Rs.5,00,000/- (Five Lakh) before the trial Court under protest.
No cheating was committed by him.
It is a case of business transaction between the parties and a false and manufactured FIR has been lodged.
Offence is triable by Judicial Magistrate First Class.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as learned counsel for the objector has opposed grant of bail on the ground that applicant has criminal background of same nature of cases.
Therefore, they have prayed for rejection of the bail application.
5. In this case, offence is triable by Judicial Magistrate First Class.
Applicant has already deposited Rs.5,00,000/- before the trial Court under protest.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant - Ashish Rajak b e released on bail subject to furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
8. It is made clear that trial Court shall pass appropriate order about the disbursement of amount so deposited by applicant in the final outcome of the case.
Certified copy as per rules.
